$e*d-1=k*\phi(n)$
$k=\frac{e*d-1}{\phi(n)}<\frac{e*\phi(n)-1}{\phi(n)}=e-\frac{1}{\phi(n)}<e$
$k\in(1,e)$
Blasting k yields phi, which can be approximately equal to n
Pq is two adjacent prime numbers. If phi is squared, a number greater than p will be obtained. Find the previous prime number of this number to obtain p, and the next prime number is q

```py
from Crypto.Util.number import *
from sympy import nextprime, prevprime
import gmpy2

e = 0x10001
c = 
d = 
for i in range(1, e):
    if (e*d-1) % i != 0:
        continue
    phi = (e*d-1)//i
    p = gmpy2.iroot(phi, 2)[0]
    p = prevprime(p)
    q = nextprime(p)
    if (p-1)*(q-1) == phi:
        n = p*q
        print(long_to_bytes(pow(c, d, n)).decode())
        break
```
